fulfillment_judgment.auxiliary_material: The study included mouse models where antibiotic depletion reduced serum butyrate and tumor progression was observed; butyrate supplementation restored efficacy. In vitro assays showed butyrate increased IFN-γ and TNF-α production in CD8+ T cells upon TCR stimulation. The study did not measure metabolite concentrations directly within human tumor tissue (TME), nor did it report absolute quantitative concentrations (e.g., μM, ng/mg) for human samples, only relative abundance comparisons between groups.
fulfillment_judgment.outline_action: Identify primary clinical studies that perform targeted metabolomics (LC-MS/MS or similar) specifically on resected human tumor tissue samples from ICI-treated patients, ensuring they report absolute concentration values (e.g., nmol/g tissue) and correlate these with response outcomes (ORR/PFS/OS). Search for studies involving paired tumor-tissue and serum/tumor-serum analysis.
fulfillment_judgment.remaining_gap: The gap requires primary studies reporting absolute quantitative concentrations of microbial metabolites measured directly in human tumor tissue (TME) or paired tumor-serum samples. This study only reports serum levels (relative comparisons, no absolute values provided in text) and does not provide measurements from human tumor tissue biopsies.
fulfillment_judgment.useful_material: The study performed targeted metabolomics (GC-MS/MS) on serum samples from NSCLC patients treated with anti-PD-1 therapy. It reported that responders had significantly higher serum levels of acetic acid, propionic acid, and butyric acid compared to non-responders. The study also found a positive correlation between serum butyric acid levels and PD-1 expression on circulating CD8+ T cells. Mechanistic experiments in vitro and in vivo demonstrated that butyrate enhances anti-PD-1 efficacy by promoting histone H3K27 acetylation at the Pdcd1 and Cd28 promoters in CD8+ T cells and enhancing TCR signaling (PLCγ1 phosphorylation).
